title: Comparison of two ring clocks: joint readings, rates and environment coupling

key_results.statement: Propagator of a minimal ring clock: $\langle m'|e^{-iC_K\mu}|m\rangle=u_N(m'-m-\mu/\lambda_0)$, $u_N(y)=N^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}e^{2\pi iky/N}$, $|u_N|^2=P_N(y)=\sin^2(\pi y)/(N^2\sin^2(\pi y/N))$.
$P_N(y)=1$ iff $y\in N\mathbb Z$; a clock started at $|m\rangle$ has a certain reading at $\mu$ iff $\mu/\lambda_0=n\in\mathbb Z$, with outcome $m+n \bmod N$.
Two free clocks: $p(m_1,m_2;\lambda)=P_{N_1}(m_1-\lambda/\lambda_{01})\,P_{N_2}(m_2-\lambda/\lambda_{02})$; the readings are independent.
Rate ratio $\rho:=\lambda_{01}/\lambda_{02}$: the number of places $K_2$ advances per place of $K_1$.
For $\rho=p/q$ (coprime), both readings are certain exactly at $\lambda=j\lambda_c$, $j\ge1$, $\lambda_c=q\lambda_{01}=p\lambda_{02}$, with readings $(jq \bmod N_1, jp \bmod N_2)$.
The set of $\lambda>0$ with both readings certain is nonempty iff $\lambda_{01}/\lambda_{02}\in\mathbb Q$.
At $\lambda=n\lambda_{01}$, $K_1$ reads $n \bmod N_1$ with certainty and $K_2$ is distributed as $P_{N_2}(m_2-n\rho)$.

Most probable reading of $K_2$ at $\lambda=n\lambda_{01}$: the integer nearest to $n\rho$ mod $N_2$ (both neighbours if $n\rho\in\mathbb Z+1/2$), with probability $P_{N_2}(\delta_n)$, $\delta_n$ the distance of $n\rho$ to $\mathbb Z$.

The offset $\Delta=m_2-m_1$ is reproduced with probability $P_=(\lambda-\lambda_s)$, equal to 1 iff $\lambda\in\lambda_s+\lambda_0\mathbb Z_{>0}$: one joint reading synchronizes identical clocks up to the recorded offset.
Clock in an eigenvector $|b\rangle$ of $B$ and $C_E$: $V_{K_1}(\lambda)=e^{-iC_b\lambda}|0\rangle\langle 0|e^{iC_b\lambda}$ with $C_b=C_{K_1}+bA$.
$K_1$ coupled by $A\otimes B$ is self-driven iff $B=0$ or $A\in\mathbb R\mathbb 1$; otherwise not.
$C_{K_1}+bA$ is a minimal ring clock contract with $N_1$ places for all $b\in\mathfrak B$ ($|\mathfrak B|\ge2$) iff $A=\gamma C_{K_1}$, $\gamma\in\mathbb R$, $1+\gamma b>0$ on $\mathfrak B$.
Two clocks in one environment with $A_i=\gamma_i C_{K_i}$: $\rho(b)=\rho\,(1+\gamma_2 b)/(1+\gamma_1 b)$.
$\rho(b)$ is the same for all $b\in\mathfrak B$ iff $\gamma_1=\gamma_2$, and then $\rho(b)=\rho$.

definitions.name: effective clock contract in an environment eigenvector

open_issues: Readings lie in Z_N, so (4.5) and (4.8) give advances and the nearest integer to nρ only modulo N_i; recovering ρ itself needs a count of turns, not derived.
Statistics of a sequence of joint readings of two different clocks (each reading collapses K2 by (2.14)) is not derived.
Environment states that are superpositions of eigenvectors of B are out of scope; the view of K1 is then not pure.
Choosing reading values of λ and comparing at equal λ uses the order of λ (criterion 8); the meaning of γ1 = γ2 for criteria 4–6 is not addressed.

consistency_checks.check: N = 2: P_2(y) = cos²(πy/2), coincidence probability 1 − sin²(πx)/2 with minimum 1/2, both half-integer places with probability 1/2
λ01 = λ02 (ρ = 1): common certain set λ01·Z>0, K2 certain at every tick of K1, coincidence probability 1 there
Dimensions and b = 0: γb dimensionless, λ01(b) has the dimension of λ, b = 0 and γ = 0 recover the free self-driven clock
